---
title: "Welcome"
---

::: lead
A practical, start-to-finish walkthrough of preprocessing 10X Chromium single-cell multiome data for zebrafish using the enhanced transcriptome annotations from the Lawson Lab.
:::

## Who this is for

You have multiome FASTQs from zebrafish, you want to run against a custom annotation (i.e., one or more custom genes included), and you need to get from raw reads to a joint object you can actually analyze.

This vignette will walk you through building a suitable `GRanges` reference for your ATAC modality, pre-processing and quality control of both the RNA and ATAC modalities, and the construction of a joint weighted-nearest-neighbor (WNN) embedding.

## What you need before you start

| Requirement | Notes |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Cell Ranger ARC | Ran by Genomic Shared Resources |
| Genome FASTA | GRCz11 |
| Transcript annotation | Lawson Lab GTF, built against a specific Ensembl release |
| Raw data | Paired GEX and ATAC FASTQs from the same library |

## Chapters

1.  **Introduction**
2.  **Building GRanges reference**
3.  **RNA pre-processing and QC**

Additional chapters are in progress. Read in order; each assumes the decisions made before it.

## Conventions

::: callout-note
Notes flag context that is useful but not required to follow the steps.
:::

::: callout-warning
Warnings flag the failure modes that produce plausible-looking but wrong output. These are the ones worth reading carefully.
:::

Shell commands are shown in full with real paths from the worked example. Substitute your own rather than copying verbatim.
